summary: The neutral stance held up. SPY fell about 0.38% on the day (spy_return 0.00376 vs 0.00761 the day before) with the regime still intact (SPY 6.49% above its 200-day in the packet). The held US broad ETFs lost ground (VOO -0.86%, VTI -0.58%) while defensive and quality holdings rose (WMT +2.88%, FAST +2.99%, VRSN +3.0%, IDXX +2.32%) and bonds firmed (IEF +0.68%, BND +0.17%). That matches the neutral, defensive-leaning read. The bond preference (IEF 21d +1.92%, TLT 21d +3.94%) also paid. The PM agreed with neutral and rejected the VXUS buy, citing my call to prefer US core over international (VXUS 21d -2.06%, 63d -1.03% vs SPY +4.39%). The book closed +1.27% since inception vs SPY +0.38%, and +1.03% vs SPY -0.38% since the version-4 start on 10-28. The one counter-signal is that the shadow portfolio (about 99% invested) beat the agent (88.1% invested) since inception, 5.41% vs 1.27%, so cautious appetite has cost return; this is a sizing question, not a stance error, because the stance was never risk-off.
update: Keep neutral. Defensive and quality names carried the day and the packet's reads on bonds and on US core vs international were not contradicted. Two things to weigh next time. (1) The agent's cash drag against the shadow (invested 88.1% vs 99.0%) shows that a neutral call should not by itself justify holding back deployment when the 200-day regime is intact; I should say explicitly how much appetite neutral supports. (2) The PM used my international call as a reason to reject a small VXUS buy, so I should state the evidence and strength behind that call (VXUS 21d -2.06%, 63d -1.03%) in case it gets treated as a rule. Watch items unchanged: SPY close below its 200-day (about 725), RSP turning negative on the 21-day return (now +3.79%), a further rise in long yields (TLT 21d +3.94% but still 2.73% under its 200-day), and the XLC weakness (5d -5.35%).
